requirement: NKT are T cells carrying rearranged TCRs, distinct from NK cells and not a mixed-cell hybrid.
The illustrated iNKT receptor recognizes a suitable CD1d-displayed lipid; conventional peptide-directed TCRs use peptide-HLA. Both require a display form.
The iNKT example places lipid tails within CD1d pockets with a head group exposed for recognition; it is qualitative rather than an atomic docking reconstruction.
CD1d dependence is different from conventional peptide-HLA dependence; classical HLA loss does not establish CD1d, its antigen or effective NKT function.
One iNKT lipid example does not define all type-II targets, receptor repertoires or functions.
An NK-associated marker alone does not identify the CD1d-restricted NKT population.
Invariant or semi-invariant receptor usage does not mean every receptor chain or function is identical.
Recognition-family identity and a cell count do not establish protective function, useful killing, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.
Gamma-delta T cells have gamma/delta TCR chains and remain a T-cell family, distinct from NK and conventional alpha-beta cells.
The depicted Vgamma9Vdelta2 mechanism is subset-limited and does not define Vdelta1 or every gamma-delta TCR.
BTN2A1 directly contacts part of the Vgamma9-bearing receptor and cooperates with BTN3A1 in phosphoantigen-linked activation.
Target-cell phosphoantigens are intracellular metabolites, rather than a free peptide or metabolite sitting in a conventional HLA groove.
The dashed additional receptor contact is schematic; the historical Rigau mechanism leaves an additional interaction to resolve and is not a current atomic-structure claim.
Conventional peptide-HLA independence is not universal for all gamma-delta receptors; a receptor-specific HLA requirement must keep its own scope.
An added CAR has a separate surface-target requirement and is not a definition of the native gamma-delta TCR, source or manufacturing method.
An HLA-low tumor lacking target X does not become target-positive because the cell product is gamma-delta; native recognition remains a separate hypothesis.
Two recognition routes do not automatically establish escape prevention, useful native killing, trafficking, safety or clinical benefit.
Native and engineered recognition need separately attributed activation and functional measurements, rather than identification from a receptor name or stain.
Target-positive and target-negative comparisons, matched cells without the CAR and suitable receptor blocking help attribute a measured response to its route.
